chunks: The palm trees that you cut down or left standing intact was by God's dispensation, so that He might disgrace the transgressors.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Muslims cut down the palm trees during the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa?
ai.summary: This verse, often cited in the context of the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa, highlights the permissibility of *Kharr* (cutting enemy trees) as a tactical measure to weaken their resources and morale. Shia scholars emphasize that this act was not merely destructive but a divinely sanctioned strategy to disgrace the *Fasiqun* (transgressors) who had previously uprooted the Muslims' palm trees, illustrating the principle of reciprocal justice in warfare.
